lessons.bridge_to_teach: Prove a synthetic minimum under fixed start/end, fixed T>0, constant positive G and unrestricted absolutely continuous paths with square-integrable velocity. Write v=vbar+delta, vbar=displacement/T and integral delta=0. Then J=T vbar^T G vbar+integral delta^T G delta. This supplies a lower bound reached by constant velocity if that path is admissible.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For displacement(2,0)L,T=2T_units and the same G, vbar=(1,0)L/T and lower bound4/T. Straight path attains4/T; dogleg has8/T. For two equal-duration segments vbar+delta and vbar-delta, excess=2 delta^T G delta>=0. Thus this declared problem has lower=upper=4/T,gap0.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For delta=(0,1)L/T, excess4/T reproduces the dogleg. If duration is changed to4T with the same displacement, straight speed halves and cost becomes2/T; it is a different optimization problem. If an obstacle excludes the straight path,4/T remains a lower bound but attainment is not established.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Comparing only two routes does not prove a global minimum; the decomposition proves it under the stated class. Do not substitute a different historical maximum-residual objective or these toy bounds for the named source least-cost certificate.
